record.paper_title: Open problems in ageing science: A roadmap for biogerontology
record.original_question: During ageing, in which contexts are senescent cells beneficial and in which contexts are they detrimental?

evidence.quote: Which and when are senescent cells beneficial and detrimental?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A senescent cell is a somatic cell that has entered a stable cell-cycle arrest while remaining metabolically active, typically exhibiting markers such as elevated p16^INK4a and p21^CIP1 expression, persistent DNA-damage response signalling, lysosomal senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, and the secretion of a characteristic senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) consisting of cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and matrix-remodelling proteases. Senescent cells accumulate in mammalian tissues with chronological ageing and have been implicated in both physiological processes (such as embryonic patterning, wound healing, and tumour suppression) and pathological processes (such as chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and age-related tissue dysfunction).

Identify and characterize, across mammalian tissues and life stages, the precise biological contexts — specifying cell type of origin, inducing stimulus (e.g. replicative exhaustion, oncogene activation, oxidative or genotoxic stress, developmental cue), tissue microenvironment, duration of persistence, and composition of the SASP — under which the presence of senescent cells confers a net beneficial effect on organismal health, and the contexts under which the presence of senescent cells confers a net detrimental effect. In particular, determine: (i) which subtypes of senescent cells (defined by molecular signature and origin) are beneficial versus detrimental; (ii) at which temporal windows during development, adulthood, and ageing each role predominates; and (iii) the mechanistic determinants (intrinsic or microenvironmental) that switch a senescent cell between beneficial and detrimental functions.
artifact.status_search_result: The roles of senescent cells in ageing — beneficial (development, wound healing, tumour suppression) versus detrimental (chronic inflammation, fibrosis, age-related pathology) — remain an actively investigated open question in biogerontology. Current reviews continue to emphasize context-dependence and heterogeneity of senescent cells, and the precise contextual mapping is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Cellular senescence: from physiology to pathology
status_evidence.snippet: Senescent cells exert context-dependent beneficial and detrimental effects; their precise roles in ageing remain incompletely understood.
status_evidence.claim: The dual roles of senescent cells in ageing remain an open and actively studied question.
